Cloud Data Migration Playbook
Practice: Technology Advisory
/
Audience: Engagement Leads
/
Version 1.4
Overview
This playbook outlines Acme Consulting's standard approach to migrating a client's on-premises
data infrastructure to a cloud platform. It is intended as a reference for engagement leads scoping a
migration workstream, not as a substitute for a client-specific migration plan, which should always be
produced during discovery.
Phase 1: Discovery and Assessment
Every migration engagement begins with a two-to-four week discovery phase that inventories the
client's existing systems, data volumes, and integration points. A common mistake in early-stage
estimates is underweighting integration complexity relative to raw data volume; a small database
with twenty downstream integrations is typically a harder migration than a large database with two.
Discovery should produce a system inventory, a data classification summary noting any regulated or
sensitive data categories, and a preliminary risk register. Engagements that skip a formal risk
register during discovery are disproportionately likely to encounter unplanned schedule slippage
during the cutover phase.
Phase 2: Migration Strategy Selection
Three strategies are commonly used, and the right choice depends on the client's tolerance for
downtime and the complexity of the source system. A lift-and-shift approach moves data with
minimal transformation and is fastest, but carries forward any existing schema problems. A
re-platform approach modernizes the schema during migration and is the most common choice for
clients with known data quality issues. A parallel-run strategy operates both systems simultaneously
for a transition period and is recommended when downtime tolerance is near zero, such as for
transaction-processing systems.
Phase 3: Execution
Migrations should always be executed in batches rather than as a single cutover, even for smaller
datasets, since batching allows validation checkpoints between stages and limits the blast radius of
any single failure. Each batch should be validated against source-system checksums before the next
batch begins, and a rollback plan should exist for every batch, not only for the final cutover.
Client communication during execution matters as much as the technical work. We recommend a
daily status update during active migration windows, even on days with no notable progress, since
silence during a migration is one of the most common sources of client anxiety on these
engagements.
Phase 4: Validation and Cutover
Before final cutover, run a full reconciliation between source and target systems covering record
counts, checksums on a sampled basis, and functional testing of downstream reports or applications
that depend on the migrated data. Known data quality issues identified during discovery should be
remediated before cutover wherever feasible, rather than migrated as-is, since fixing them
Cloud Data Migration Playbook - Page 1

post-migration is typically more expensive once the data is in active use.
Common Pitfalls
- Underestimating integration complexity relative to data volume during initial scoping.
- Treating discovery as optional or compressing it to save time, which increases risk later.
- Migrating known-bad data as-is instead of scheduling a cleansing sprint before cutover.
- Insufficient client communication during execution, leading to avoidable stakeholder anxiety.
- Skipping a rollback plan for intermediate batches, not just the final cutover.
Cloud Data Migration Playbook - Page 2

Quarterly Engagement Report . Q2 2026
Prepared for: Client Executive Sponsor
/
Prepared by: Engagement Lead
/
July 2026
Executive Summary
This quarter's engagement focused on completing the data migration workstream and beginning
discovery for the reporting dashboard workstream. Overall the engagement remains on schedule
and within the originally approved budget, with total spend at 48% of the annual contract value
against a planned 52% at this point in the calendar.
Key Milestones Completed
- Legacy database schema fully mapped to the new platform, covering all 14 core tables identified
in the Q1 discovery phase.
- 92% of historical records migrated and validated against source-system checksums.
- Stakeholder interviews completed for the dashboard workstream, covering finance, operations,
and regional sales leadership.
- Security review of the new platform's access control model completed with no critical findings.
Risks and Mitigations
The remaining 8% of historical records contain data quality issues inherited from a prior system
migration in 2019, primarily duplicate customer records and inconsistent date formatting in the
transaction history tables. Migrating these records as-is would propagate known errors into the new
platform's reporting layer.
We recommend a two-week data cleansing sprint before final cutover rather than migrating these
known-bad records as-is. This would push the final cutover date back by approximately ten business
days but avoids a more costly remediation effort after go-live, when the affected records would
already be in active use across multiple downstream reports.
A secondary, lower-severity risk is dashboard workstream scope: two of the five stakeholder groups
interviewed requested reporting capabilities beyond the originally scoped set of dashboards. We
recommend treating these as a Phase 2 addition rather than expanding the current workstream, to
avoid schedule slippage on the core deliverables.
Budget Status
Year-to-date spend is tracking under the planned burn rate, primarily due to the data migration
workstream completing ahead of the original estimate. We recommend reallocating the resulting
budget headroom toward the recommended data cleansing sprint rather than returning it, since the
cleansing work directly reduces downstream risk on the reporting workstream.
Next Quarter Priorities
- Complete data cleansing sprint and final cutover to the new platform.
- Deliver first draft of the reporting dashboard wireframes for stakeholder review.
- Begin user acceptance testing with the finance team, targeting a two-week testing window.
- Revisit Phase 2 scope discussion with stakeholders once core dashboards are stable.
Quarterly Engagement Report - Q2 2026 - Page 1

Team and Staffing
The engagement team remains staffed at three consultants and one engagement lead through the
end of Q3, which matches the original staffing plan. We do not anticipate needing to add headcount
for the data cleansing sprint, since the work is well-scoped and can be absorbed by the current team
without extending the timeline further.
One staffing change to note: our data engineer on this account will be rotating off at the start of Q3
to support a new engagement, and will be replaced by a consultant of equivalent seniority who has
already begun shadowing the current cutover planning to ensure a smooth handoff.
Client Feedback
Informal feedback gathered during this quarter's stakeholder interviews was positive overall, with
several finance team members specifically noting that the migration workstream's validation process
gave them confidence in the new platform's data accuracy. The primary piece of constructive
feedback was a request for more advance notice ahead of scheduled maintenance windows, which
we have incorporated into the communication plan for the upcoming cutover.
Quarterly Engagement Report - Q2 2026 - Page 2

Acme Consulting - Remote Work Policy
Effective Date: January 1, 2026 / Owner: People Operations I Version 3.2
1. Purpose
This policy establishes guidelines for employees working remotely, either full-time or on a hybrid
schedule, to ensure consistent expectations around availability, communication, data security, and
equipment across every team at Acme Consulting. It applies to all full-time and part-time employees,
and does not apply to independent contractors, whose remote work terms are governed separately
by their statement of work.
2. Eligibility
Employees who have completed their 90-day probationary period and whose role does not require
regular physical presence on client premises are eligible to apply for a remote work arrangement.
Client-facing consultants staffed on engagements that require on-site work retain a hybrid schedule
determined by the engagement lead, and eligibility for those roles is reassessed at the start of each
new engagement.
New hires joining in a fully remote capacity are exempt from the 90-day waiting period, provided the
remote arrangement was agreed upon during the offer stage and is documented in the offer letter.
3. Core Hours and Availability
All remote employees must be available and responsive between 10:00 AM and 3:00 PM in their
local time zone, regardless of which time zone they are working from. Outside of core hours,
employees may structure their schedule flexibly, provided total weekly hours meet their role's
expectations and any standing client meetings are attended.
Employees traveling across time zones for more than three consecutive business days should notify
their manager in advance so that core-hour expectations can be temporarily adjusted.
4. Equipment and Security
The company will provide a laptop, external monitor, and VPN access for approved remote
employees. All company data must remain on company-issued devices and must never be stored on
personal cloud storage accounts, personal email, or removable media. Employees connecting from
public Wi-Fi networks, such as those in cafes or airports, are required to use the company VPN at all
times.
Lost or stolen equipment must be reported to IT Security within four hours of discovery so that
device credentials can be revoked and remote wipe procedures initiated.
5. Home Office Stipend
Eligible employees may claim up to $500 per year toward home office equipment such as desks,
chairs, monitor arms, and lighting, submitted through the standard expense reimbursement process
with itemized receipts. Stipend claims for the current calendar year must be submitted no later than
December 15, and unused stipend amounts do not roll over to the following year.
6. Performance and Review
Acme Consulting - Remote Work Policy - Page 1

Remote work arrangements are reviewed annually by the employee's manager as part of the
standard performance cycle, and may be modified or revoked at any time if availability,
communication, or performance expectations are not being met. Managers are expected to
document any concerns and provide a 30-day improvement window before revoking a remote
arrangement, except in cases involving a security policy violation.
7. Frequently Asked Questions
- Can I work from another country temporarily? Yes, for up to 20 business days per year with
manager approval and an IT Security review of the destination country's data regulations.
- Does the home office stipend cover internet bills? No, ongoing utilities such as internet or
electricity are not covered by the one-time equipment stipend.
- Who do I contact about VPN issues? IT Helpdesk, available during core hours via the internal
support portal.
Acme Consulting - Remote Work Policy - Page 2

Case Study: Retail Supply Chain Optimization
Industry: Grocery Retail
/
Engagement Length: 7 months
/
Practice: Operations
Client Background
The client is a mid-sized regional grocery retailer operating 45 stores across three states, with an
annual revenue of approximately $310 million. The company had grown through acquisition over the
prior decade, resulting in inconsistent inventory practices between store clusters that had originally
belonged to different regional chains.
Challenge
The client's inventory forecasting relied on spreadsheets updated manually by each store manager,
with no shared visibility across locations. This led to frequent stockouts of high-demand items during
weekend peaks and significant overstock of perishable goods early in the week, resulting in an
estimated $2.3 million in annual waste, primarily in the produce and dairy categories.
A secondary challenge was staff time: store managers reported spending eight to ten hours per
week on manual counts and reorder spreadsheets, time that could otherwise go toward
customer-facing activities during a period when the client was also trying to improve in-store service
scores.
Approach
Our team implemented a centralized demand forecasting system that ingests point-of-sale data
nightly and generates automated purchase order recommendations for each store location, factoring
in day-of-week seasonality, local weather forecasts, and historical promotional lift. We also
